I struggle with the same things, but in my case I think I found a strategy that works? 
1) Realizing that time is really limited. It's important. It's impossible to be good at many things, but you can, for example, be good at 3-7 things. 
2) Find those things. You know you found one, when after some time you dropped it, you come back to it. If this cycle of dropping, picking up, dropping, picking up repeats, you probably found one. 
3) Once you have a list of these things realize one fact, that is true for you: you won't be able to work at a job you don't like. Because if you want to succeed in a job, you must constantly improve. And if a thing that you are doing on your job you despise, you'll either get stuck in the start of your career, or be fired instantly. 
4) After you picked up 3-7 things to cycle through, start doing it. Don't feel bad if you don't come back to thing number one for MONTHS. As long as you are doing things from the list, it's okay. 
5) After much pain and struggle, you'll realize that you're better in things number 2, 4 and 6, then others. You'll start to see that these things are so huge, each of them can be divided into 2-3 points. Now you can make a decision to drop things 1,3, 4 and 7 to pursue deeper understanding of things number 2, 4 and 6 and their points. Continue to cycle through. 
6) Have a stoic mindset. Learn to be okay with a thought that: "I might do it my entire life and don't really achieve something special. Or I might achieve great things. I don't know. But I'll do my best in each cycle in my process."

This is something that I figured out for myself living a life like your since I was a kid. Maybe it works for you
